Q: Case expression taking aliased names value A:

You need to fix the quotes by converting them to single quotes, and use aggregation per each conditional expression rather than the alias ("Cars bought") within the current case

SELECT custname,
       COUNT(carserial) AS "Cars bought",
       CASE WHEN COUNT(carserial) = 1 THEN
                 'One time buyer'
            WHEN COUNT(carserial) = 2 THEN
                 'Twice buyer' 
            WHEN COUNT(carserial) >= 3 THEN
                 'Frequent buyer'
            END
  FROM SI.car
 WHERE carmake = 'MERCEDES'
 GROUP BY custname

Q: PostgreSQL: Will DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED prevent this race condition? A:

If I declare the foreign key as DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED, then the foreign key will be evaluated by T2 only when it commits, and the new row should be in B by that time. So, do I understand correctly it will help?

I don't think it will help. It doesn't affect how and what gets locked, only when - it will do the same "lookup->request row lock->wait->acquire->realise the row is gone" thing, just at a later time.

It might help only if the relative timing of T1 and T2 is somehow coupled, synced or coordinated, in a way that lets you trust that postponing T2's check gives just enough time, every time, for T1 to complete before T2's referential integrity check comes knocking.

If you're trying to nudge the timing, just making it deferrable could already shift things around even if it's initially immediate - that pushes things back from mid-statement to post-statement. Here you can find some more details on why immediate can actually end up the 2nd most immediate constraint check, non-deferrables being more or really immediate:

  • Why does PostgreSQL check a DEFERRABLE INITIALLY IMMEDIATE constraint after each statement?

But if the problem is with the isolation level, will changing it help, too? Will either? Will both? What is better?

Changing the isolation level will not side-step the problem or change anything in the locking behaviour at the root of your problem. Combining it with deferrability doesn't change things. You could only use it to accommodate the retry logic suggested in @Laurenz Albe's great answer.

If not isolation level and/or deferrability, what else could help?
(not a quote, I'm just assuming this should naturally follow)

You could start T2 by acquiring a row lock in B, on the thing you're referencing from A:

select from b where id=$1
for key share of b /*nowait*/;
  • If there's a conflicting T1 in progress, T2 waits at that initial statement and regardless of whether that row ends up updated, reinserted, deleted, once it gets the lock, T2 proceeds to run the insert with a guarantee that nobody can now interfere.
  • If a T1 appears while T2 is in progress, it's T1 that will have to wait for the lock held by T2.

You can uncomment nowait and use it to implement similar retry logic to the one mentioned by Laurenz - it'll cause T2 to fail if a conflicting T1 is in progress.

This example is also a reminder that for row-locking selects, exists() conditions and a few other things, you can have an empty select list.

Q: Group By with Case expression A:

How about the following:

COUNT OF ORDERS

select      year([Date]) as yr,
            month([Date]) as monthofyr,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=1) and (day([Date])<=3),1,0)) as days1to3,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=4) and (day([Date])<=6),1,0)) as days4to6,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=7) and (day([Date])<=9),1,0)) as days7to9,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=10) and (day([Date])<=12),1,0)) as days10to12,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=13) and (day([Date])<=15),1,0)) as days13to15,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=16) and (day([Date])<=18),1,0)) as days16to18,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=19) and (day([Date])<=21),1,0)) as days19to21,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=22) and (day([Date])<=24),1,0)) as days22to24,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=25) and (day([Date])<=27),1,0)) as days25to27,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=28) and (day([Date])<=31),1,0)) as days28to31
from        tbl
where       [Date] between x and y
group by    year([Date]),
            month([Date])

Replace x and y with your date range.

The last group is days 28 to 31 of the month, so it may contain 4 days' worth of orders, for months that have 31 days.

THE ABOVE IS A COUNT OF ORDERS.

If you want the SUM of the order amounts:

SUM OF ORDER AMOUNTS

select      year([Date]) as yr,
            month([Date]) as monthofyr,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=1) and (day([Date])<=3),order,0)) as days1to3,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=4) and (day([Date])<=6),order,0)) as days4to6,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=7) and (day([Date])<=9),order,0)) as days7to9,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=10) and (day([Date])<=12),order,0)) as days10to12,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=13) and (day([Date])<=15),order,0)) as days13to15,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=16) and (day([Date])<=18),order,0)) as days16to18,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=19) and (day([Date])<=21),order,0)) as days19to21,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=22) and (day([Date])<=24),order,0)) as days22to24,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=25) and (day([Date])<=27),order,0)) as days25to27,
            sum(iif((day([Date])>=28) and (day([Date])<=31),order,0)) as days28to31
from        tbl
where       [Date] between x and y
group by    year([Date]),
            month([Date])

Q: Does passing a 64-byte readonly struct repeatedly cause copying overhead compared to a class reference? A:

Will PersonOrdinals be copied on every MapPerson() call

Yes

under what circumstances would changing it to in-parameter avoid measurable overhead compared to using a class reference instead

The best way to determine this is to measure. Using large structs that are passed by reference have some benefits in some scenarios, a typical example is games that are very performance sensitive and want to avoid heap allocations as much as possible.

Do note that passing a reference to a struct and passing a class reference should have exactly the same performance at the point of the method call. Any performance difference would be due to things like allocation cost, GC costs, memory locality etc.

For a typical line-of-business application I doubt you could measure any difference between using a struct + in-parameter vs just using a class. Chances are that anything you are doing with the database will have a far larger impact on performance than this.

Q: Convert OR operator to case expression A:

CASE is probably not the best pick to express such boolean logic. MySQL, however, understands tuple equality, so you could rewrite this:

AND (
    (t_product.a_active = 1 AND t_product.a_mpactive = 0)
    OR (t_product.a_active = 0 AND t_product.a_mpactive = 1)
    OR (t_product.a_active = 0 AND t_product.a_mpactive = 0)
)

As:

AND (t_product.a_active, t_product.a_mpactive) in ( (1, 0), (0, 1), (0, 0) )

That will make the query neater, but not necessarily faster. Under the hood, the optimizer rewrites the query and both expressions might be ultimately interpreted similarly.

If we were to phrase this with CASE, we would have to wrap it somehow, to make it look like a predicate. Something like:

AND 1 = CASE
    WHEN t_product.a_active = 1 AND t_product.a_mpactive = 0 THEN 1
    WHEN t_product.a_active = 0 AND t_product.a_mpactive = 1 THEN 1
    WHEN t_product.a_active = 0 AND t_product.a_mpactive = 0 THEN 1
END

... And, for what it's worth... If both columns always store non-null boolean values (0/1), then the condition is simpler phrased as a negation:

WHERE NOT (t_product.a_active = 1 AND t_product.a_mpactive = 1)

Or:

WHERE (t_product.a_active, t_product.a_mpactive) not in ( (1, 1) )

Q: Linux - timeout on disconnected send A:

I've been working on a solution to this or something very similar in the past 3 weeks. Here is what I observed:

  • Safari is streaming an MP4 file with HTTP Range and suddenly sends TLS notify_close + FIN

  • The server was busy reading and sending file blocks and did not call recv to catch the FIN

  • The client has fully abandoned the connection and sends RST to each server packet in flight

  • ISP NAT delivers the first RST to server and immediately forgets the NAT session

  • That RST packet is ignored, because it's sequence number is before TLS notify_close + FIN

  • The client keeps sending RST with old sequence, because ACK from server is still in flight

  • Eventually the client sends a final RST with correct sequence number once ACK is received

  • All of these packets are dropped by incorrectly functioning NAT on the ISP / 5G carrier

  • The server has no idea that the socket is closed, it received FIN and sees CLOSE_WAIT

  • The server knows it cannot receive, but still believes it can send data, so

  • send remains blocked for a very long time and it makes many retransmissions

Note: on a properly functioning network, the final RST from client would be delivered to the server causing send to return EPIPE.

Fix: make sure the server calls recv while sending to detect FIN from the client, then abort send

Workaround:

  • If the receiving thread is busy reading a file, make send non-blocking and use poll

  • POLLOUT | POLLERR | POLLHUP if not currently receiving, add POLLIN

  • It gets tricky when no storage is available to receive inside the function sending data

  • For a TLS connection the read BIO may be used, else we need a temp buffer

  • that will be consumed by the receiving task later

  • Once TLS notify_close arrives or recv returns 0, abandon the connection

  • set SO_SNDTIMEO to a very low value and don't expect any replay from the client

  • Doing this in a send function is ugly, but helps when the receiving code is doing other work
